items.title: Public Meeting to Consider A Zoning Amendment
Zoning Amendment Application (RZ005-2025), for lands known
notes: municipally as 6949 Wellington Rd 7, Nichol.

For Information regarding the Application see our website Mayor Watters indicated the purpose of this public meeting is to present and receive public input regarding a proposed zoning by-law amendment on the subject land known as 6949 Wellington Road 7, in the former Township of Nichol.

He noted the purpose of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to change the zoning from “A” Agricultural and “EP” Environment Protection to “A” Agricultural Exception and “EP” Environment Protection.

The effect of the proposed zoning by-law amendment is to implement zoning regulations necessary to establish a shop for the repair and maintenance of farm drainage equipment as an agriculture-related use.

Mayor Watters indicated if a person or public body would otherwise have an ability to appeal the decision of the Township of Centre Wellington to the Ontario Land Tribunal (OLT) but the person or public body does not make oral submissions at a public meeting or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by- law is passed, the person or public body is not entitled to appeal the decision.

Mayor Watters stated if a person or public body does not make oral submission at the public meeting, or make written submissions to the Township of Centre Wellington before the by-law is passed, the person or public body may not be added as the party to the hearing of an appeal before the OLT unless, in the opinion of the Tribunal, there are reasonable grounds to do so.

Mayor Watters advised if anyone wishes to be notified of the adoption of the proposed zoning by-law amendment, a written request must be filed with the Municipal Clerk, Township of Centre Wellington, 1 MacDonald Square, Elora, ON N0B 1S0.

The Municipal Clerk advised notice was mailed to prescribed persons, agencies and public bodies on or before July 10, 2025. She indicated a copy of the notice was advertised in the Wellington Advertiser on July 10, 2025, and confirmed the requirement for giving notice was completed on July 10, 2025.
Mayor Watters called on Deanna Maiden, Senior Development Planner, to introduce the application.

Deanna Maiden, Senior Development Planner indicated provided an overview of the proposal, indicating the application would implement zoning regulations necessary to establish a shop for the repair and maintenance of farm drainage equipment as an agriculture-related use..

She noted the subject property is a rural agricultural property located on the east side of Wellington County Road 7, in the northwesterly part of the Township, just southeast of the Hamlet of Alma. The subject lands are approximately 4.5 hectares in size with 455 metres of frontage along Highway 7, with a single detached dwelling and accessory buildings that support a livestock operation
Mayor Watters called on Rob Stovel to make a presentation on the application.

Rob Stovel, Stovel and Associates introduced the landowner, the applicant and the consulting team and outlined the scope of the proposal to establish a farm-related business. R. Stovel noted it is not a commercial shop, the building will be used to store and maintain large equipment and an office. He also noted the fuel onsite is for the use of the business only and not a fuel storage facility.

R. Stovel noted the remaining lands, including the house and out- buildings will be retained except for a barn that will be removed and will continue to be used for agriculture. He suggested the proposal is consistent with the Provincial Policy Statement, conforms to the County’s official plan and supports the agricultural community.

Mayor Watters invited Heather Smith, 31 Queen Street South, Alma, Ontario to speak as a delegation. She expressed concerns and posed questions regarding measures to be taken given Alma falls within the Wellhead Protection Area for Quantity (WHPA-Q) for the Township of Centre Wellington and the fuel station.
Rob Stovel indicated he will prepare a formal response to the matters raised.
Mayor Watters asked if anyone present wishes to speak to the application., there being none, he offered Council an opportunity to ask any questions of the applicant or staff.

Staff and the applicant responded to questions regarding the proposed agricultural use for the balance of the subject lands, the extent of the circulation of the application, and the conditional offer to purchase the lands.
Mayor Watters thanked everyone for attending and advised Council will be considering the by-law at a future Council meeting.
Mayor Watters declared the public meeting adjourned and called for a 2 minute recess.

items.title: Proposed Agreement: Communication Infrastructure Enhancement
notes: Report from Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer

Dan Wilson, Chief Administrative Officer provided an overview of the report, indicating The Grand 101 FM has approached Township staff, requesting assistance with funding the purchase and installation of a backup generator. He noted the agreement would allow the Township to secure dedicated airtime at a preferred fixed rate on The Grand 101 FM by funding the backup generator purchase and installation with an upfront investment of $90,230.50. Over ten years, The Grand 101 FM would repay $116,852.63 (principal amount plus 5% annual interest) through airtime, ensuring cost certainty and reliable emergency communications. This initiative supports public safety, civic engagement, and sustainable governance, with annual repayments drawn from the Office of the CAO and Communications cost centre budget annually.
